purpose: OGC-owned intake decisions for Ancient and Medieval material in three permissively licensed GlossAPI datasets. These pins govern OGC ingestion only; downstream consumers pin an OGC export rather than these upstreams.

consumer_contract.dilemma_input: public_lexicon.tsv and the associated OGC release/content hash
consumer_contract.frequency_rule: No raw GlossAPI historical frequency enters Dilemma. Only text admitted to OGC after identity, deduplication, provenance, and quality gates contributes to the public lexicon.

sources.license: CC-BY-4.0; underlying Project Gutenberg works described as public domain
sources.reason: The 214-row dataset mixes Ancient, Katharevousa, Demotic, and Modern Greek; its variety field was generated by the same external classifier under evaluation, and the dataset card says per-document source URLs are absent. Variety labels are routing hints, not admission evidence.
required_gates: Recover a stable Project Gutenberg work identifier or source URL for every candidate row.
Identify the underlying work and edition/translation; exclude Modern Greek translations from the Ancient/Medieval route.
Classify variety independently of the supplied model label.
Deduplicate at work and passage level against data/corpus before serving any row.
Write normal OGC work, edition, license, and source provenance before the yardstick rebuild.
sources.admission_output: Only independently identified Ancient/Medieval works may become locus-keyed data/corpus records; the supplied variety label is not retained as gold annotation.

sources.reason: The source is explicitly Medieval/Hellenistic Koine liturgical text and has useful title/category metadata, but it contains structural rubrics and run-together boundaries, while biblical, hymnographic, and service-book material is highly repetitive and overlaps sources OGC already serves.
required_gates: Map title/category/subcategory to a stable work or service unit and retain the GOARCH source URL.
Strip structural rubrics and page or service identifiers before tokenization.
Detect and repair or quarantine run-together sentence and section boundaries before lexical extraction.
Separate biblical quotations/readings from independently authored liturgical material.
Run exact and near-duplicate passage checks across Oktoechos tone cycles and against existing biblical, patristic, hymnographic, and liturgical works.
Prefer OGC's existing identified edition where the GlossAPI row is only a duplicate witness.
Admit unique text as locus-keyed records with explicit CC-BY-4.0 provenance.
sources.admission_output: Cleaned, deduplicated, identified passages in data/corpus; raw or duplicate-only rows contribute no token or n-gram frequency.

sources.reason: The 814 records are volume-level OCR from publications spanning 1837 to the present, mixing Modern commentary, Ancient quotations, other languages, and documented scan/OCR noise. Volume OCR cannot safely become lexical evidence without segmentation and quality review.
required_gates: Retain pdf_url and collection as immutable document provenance and recover publication date/volume identity.
Segment Ancient/Medieval primary text from Modern commentary, apparatus, bibliography, and non-Greek spans.
Measure Unicode, mixed-script, nonlexical, and unattested-form rates per segment.
Route OCR segments through OGC's existing OCR quality/review policy; never admit a whole volume by classifier label.
Deduplicate accepted primary-text segments against existing editions and quotations before serving them.
sources.admission_output: No direct corpus ingest. Only reviewed, identified primary-text segments that pass OGC OCR and dedup gates may enter data/corpus.
